title: Southern Liang
capsule: The Southern Liang (南涼, Nán Liáng, 397–414) was a Xianbei state of the Sixteen Kingdoms era, ruled by the Tufa clan — collateral relatives of the Tuoba who founded the Northern Wei — and centered in what is now northeastern Qinghai and eastern Gansu. Tufa Wugu proclaimed himself Prince of Xiping in 397; his successor Tufa Lilugu (399–402) submitted to Later Qin as a vassal; and Tufa Rutan (402–414) assumed the title King of Liang and maintained the longest reign, rotating the capital among Lianchuan, Ledu, and Xiping. By 413 the state had contracted to a few commanderies, and in 414 Western Qin forces seized the capital Ledu while Rutan was campaigning against rebel tribes; he surrendered and was subsequently poisoned by Western Qin ruler Qifu Chipan.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core political events are recorded in Chinese dynastic histories (Jin Shu, Wei Shu), but the spatial extent of Southern Liang control at any given year is imprecisely defined.
